newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Deson shrs seen strong on debut - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Deson shrs seen strong on debut - analysts.

text.p: Construction firm Deson Development International Holdings Ltd has generated strong investor interest and has the potential to see future share price gains after its trading debut on Tuesday, analysts said.
Analysts said the initial public offering (IPO) for the Hong Kong-based company which does business mainly in China was 165 times oversubscribed.
The grey market price of about HK$1.55 on Friday, compared with the issue price of HK$1.00, also showed a strong response among investors, analysts said.
"Even though its business nature is not that exciting, its debut is seen to be good in view of a strong subscription response," said Ben Kwong, director of research of Dharmala Securities.
Deson offered 75 million new shares, or 25 percent of its enlarged share capital, in an IPO in Hong Kong.
The company said it would use the net proceeds to fund its investment in the Chinese government-sponsored Economic Housing Scheme and to expand its construction business.
"We expect the shares to be fairly valued at about HK$1.80," Kwong said, adding that interest in the stock was underscored by the fact that a Japanese firm took a strategic stake in Deson.
Okabe Co Ltd, a scaffolding and structural materials maker in Japan, agreed to take a 9.4 percent stake in Deson at the issue price.
Analysts said the stock has upside potential because its price to earnings (P/E) multiple of about seven times was still cheap.

However, some analysts said uncertainty over the property market in China would cap the stock's upside in the longer run. Deson engages in building construction, interior decoration and project management in Beijing and Shanghai cities and in Shangdong, Zhejiang, Guangdong and Shenyang provinces.
